author_reading_scope: Three independent full-text treatments were retrieved: a textbook, a finite-horizon primary paper, and the controlling offline-RL review. I inspected the complete source sections relevant to the local finite-horizon trajectory-ratio, OIS/PDIS/WIS, DR, support, and offline-safety claims. The finite-horizon density factorization, OIS/PDIS expectation, both DR branches, estimator-bias calculations, and two-MDP impossibility proof are supplied locally; no source statement or citation substitutes for those proofs. The Jiang–Li proceedings PDF states Theorem 1 but does not contain a complete proof of its unbiasedness claim in the fetched 10-page text; the paper defers proof material to an appendix that is not present in this proceedings PDF.

search_and_retrieval_history.query: Jiang Li Doubly Robust Off-policy Value Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning ICML 2016 PMLR PDF
search_and_retrieval_history.outcome: Located the official PMLR proceedings page and full 10-page PDF. Inspected the finite-horizon setup, IS/WIS equations, contextual DR formula, sequential DR recursion, and Theorem 1 statement.

search_and_retrieval_history.outcome: Located the Stanford-hosted full second-edition textbook PDF. Opened all 352 pages and inspected §5.5 and Example 5.5 at the cited printed and PDF locators.

search_and_retrieval_history.outcome: Located the arXiv record and complete 43-page PDF. Inspected the design-designated distribution-shift, OPE, policy-constraint, and model-exploitation sections.

search_and_retrieval_history.outcome: Search surfaced an additional 2016 paper and its full text. It was not selected for this batch's source set, and no claim or proof below relies on it.

sources.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.

author_read_locators.locator: §5.5, printed pp. 128–129, Stanford PDF pp. 140–142: behavior/target policies, action coverage, product trajectory ratio (5.3), ordinary estimate (5.4), and weighted estimate (5.5).
author_read_locators.disposition: The discrete stationary-policy formulas and support convention are included as context. The local finite-horizon likelihood-ratio and unbiasedness arguments are proved independently.

author_read_locators.locator: §5.5, printed p. 129, Stanford PDF p. 142: zero-denominator WIS convention and the one-observation bias discussion.
author_read_locators.disposition: The estimator convention motivates the local procedure. The finite-sample bias and clipping calculations are recomputed exactly in the example.

author_read_locators.locator: Example 5.5, printed pp. 131–132, Stanford PDF pp. 144–145: one-state looping MDP and complete infinite expected-square series.
author_read_locators.disposition: This supports the warning about multiplicative trajectory weights. The authored example uses a distinct fixed finite horizon and proves an exact finite variance formula rather than claiming infinite variance.

sources.title: Nan Jiang and Lihong Li, Doubly Robust Off-policy Value Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 48

author_read_locators.locator: §3.2, PDF pp. 2–3, equations (1)–(7): fixed finite horizon, return/value convention, trajectory IS, step-wise IS, and WIS.
author_read_locators.disposition: The paper's finite-horizon estimator formulas are included. The local density argument verifies the required common-dynamics, support, propensity, and integrability hypotheses.

author_read_locators.locator: §3.3, PDF p. 3, equation (8), and §4.1, PDF pp. 3–4, equations (9)–(10): contextual and sequential doubly robust constructions.
author_read_locators.disposition: The algorithmic recursion is the source interface. The local statement fixes a terminal value of zero and nuisance inputs independent of evaluation trajectories, and its proof handles both branches separately.

author_read_locators.locator: Theorem 1, §4.2, PDF p. 4: unbiasedness statement and variance recursion; the text defers proof material to Appendix A.
author_read_locators.disposition: The fetched proceedings text supplies the theorem statement but not a complete proof of its unbiasedness assertion. No missing step is inferred from the citation; the finite-horizon proof is local.

author_read_locators.locator: §3.2.2, PDF p. 3, equations (6)–(7): WIS is described as biased and consistent.
author_read_locators.disposition: Only the finite-sample-bias warning is used. No consistency result is claimed.

sources.title: Sergey Levine, Aviral Kumar, George Tucker, and Justin Fu, Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems

author_read_locators.locator: §2.4, PDF pp. 8–9: static-data limitations, counterfactual queries, and distribution shift.
author_read_locators.disposition: The review supplies conceptual context. The finite two-MDP indistinguishability result is proved locally.

author_read_locators.locator: §3.1, PDF pp. 10–12, equations (5)–(6): OIS, PDIS, self-normalized WIS, doubly robust estimation, and their stated limitations.
author_read_locators.disposition: This source is a tutorial review and attributes formal estimator results to cited papers. It is not treated as proof of any local estimator identity.

author_read_locators.locator: §3.5, PDF pp. 15–16; §§4.3–4.4, PDF pp. 20–24: compounding weights, policy constraints, and uncertainty-based mitigation.
author_read_locators.disposition: The source supports the variance and mitigation cautions, not a universal guarantee.

author_read_locators.locator: §5.1, PDF pp. 26–28: model exploitation under state/action distribution shift.
author_read_locators.disposition: The local remark limits this to a qualitative warning and claims no generic model-based safety theorem.
